description: Decision policy for adaptive Ask vs Act behavior

act_immediately.description: Known decisions that can be made autonomously
conditions: Answer is explicitly stated in PRD
Answer is defined in existing codebase configuration
Answer follows an established project convention
examples: Test file location (defined in testing skill)

conditions: PRD implies the answer with high confidence
Existing codebase patterns clearly suggest the answer
Tech stack constraints limit options to one viable choice
Industry best practices strongly favor one option
examples: Database choice when PRD specifies document-based data (→ MongoDB)
Multi-tenancy when PRD mentions organizations/teams (→ multi-tenant)
Real-time when PRD mentions live updates (→ WebSockets)
Caching when PRD mentions high-traffic endpoints (→ Redis)
infer_and_act.requirement: Log the inference in decisions.json with confidence and source

research_first.description: Uncertain but researchable without user input
conditions: Answer can be determined by reading existing code
Answer can be determined by analyzing dependencies
examples: Best pagination strategy for a specific query pattern
Whether a library supports a required feature
Performance implications of a design choice

ask_user.description: Genuinely ambiguous or high-risk decisions requiring user input
conditions: Requirement is genuinely ambiguous (multiple valid interpretations)
High-risk architectural decision with irreversible consequences
Business logic decision that cannot be inferred from technical context
